fatal_errors: The proposed Q235 steel system does not match the target system of an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating deposited on SS316L.
It omits the governing intervention: atmospheric plasma spraying followed by a 2 h anneal, particularly the 550 °C condition.
The proposed 20–80 °C humidity exposure does not reproduce either the 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C molten-salt cyclic hot-corrosion tests.
The central grain-refinement, BCC/FCC phase, coating-defect, sluggish-diffusion, and Al/Cr-rich passive-scale mechanisms are absent.
The predicted 30% corrosion-rate increase and 20% falsification threshold are arbitrary and unsupported by cited evidence.
No prior evidence is supplied, and the retracted status of the target source is not acknowledged.
explanation: The hypothesis is a generic temperature–humidity corrosion study rather than a reconstruction of the target coating-and-annealing study. It has limited conceptual overlap through oxide-film formation and proposes a controllable factorial experiment, but it changes the substrate, intervention, exposure media, temperature regime, baselines, measurements, mechanism, and expected direction and magnitude of outcomes. The falsification rule is measurable but tests an unsupported numerical threshold rather than whether annealing-induced coating refinement and Al/Cr-rich passivation govern corrosion resistance.
